title: Reading scales
examples: How do I know what the lines mean?
Can I use this scale for liquid?
What is the biggest number I can read?

explain.say: Today we learn how to read different measuring scales. A scale helps us see exact amounts. Look at this ruler on the screen. It measures length in centimetres and millimetres.
The big numbers are the main marks. The space between two big numbers is the total length. You must always start counting from zero on the scale.
Sometimes there are smaller lines between the big marks. These small lines show smaller units of measure. For example, one big space might have ten small lines.
When measuring liquid, we use a measuring jug. We read the level at the bottom of the curve. Always read at eye level to be accurate.

draw.text: Read liquid level at eye level.

faq.q: What do the numbers on the ruler mean?
faq.a: The numbers show the length in units like centimetres or inches. You read the number that lines up with the object you measure. You might also ask, "What is the measurement?" or "How long is this?"?
asks: What do the numbers on the ruler mean?

faq.q: Do I always start at zero when measuring?
faq.a: Yes, you must always start reading from the zero mark. If you start anywhere else, your measurement will be wrong. You might also ask, "Where do I start counting?" or "Does it matter where I start?"?
asks: Do I always start at zero when measuring?
Does it matter where I start?

faq.q: How do I read a measuring jug for water?
faq.a: You look at the curved surface of the water, not the top edge. The line that matches the water level tells you the amount. You could also ask, "What is the water level?" or "How much liquid is there?"?
asks: How do I read a measuring jug for water?

faq.q: What are the small lines on the scale?
faq.a: The small lines show fractions or smaller parts of the main unit. They help us be more precise with our measurements. You might also ask, "What do the tiny lines mean?" or "How small can I measure?"?
asks: What are the small lines on the scale?
What do the tiny lines mean?

faq.q: Can I use a ruler for liquids?
faq.a: No, you should use a measuring jug for liquids. Rulers are for measuring solid length, not flowing liquids. You could also ask, "Is this ruler good for juice?" or "What tool for liquid?"?
asks: Can I use a ruler for liquids?
Is this ruler good for juice?

facts: Rulers measure straight length in units like centimetres.
Measuring jugs are used to measure liquids like water or juice.
Always read liquid levels at eye level for accuracy.
Measurements must always start counting from the zero mark.

quiz.say: If a pencil measures exactly three centimetres on a ruler, what is the correct reading?
quiz.why: The ruler shows the length directly at the three centimetre mark.

wrong.1: This is a common mistake because one centimetre equals ten millimetres.
wrong.2: This is too detailed; the simple reading is sufficient.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it does not include the correct unit of measure.

quiz.say: When measuring a bottle of juice, where should your eyes be positioned?
quiz.why: Reading at eye level stops you from reading the measurement incorrectly.

wrong.0: Looking from above can make the liquid level look higher than it really is.
wrong.1: Looking from below can make the liquid level look lower than it really is.
wrong.2: The angle you look from changes the apparent level of the liquid.

quiz.say: A scale shows a mark at 5 and the next mark at 10. If there are 5 small lines between them, what is the value of each small line?
quiz.why: You divide the total space by the number of small gaps to find the value.

wrong.0: This incorrectly reads the entire space as a single small mark.
wrong.1: This suggests the small lines have no measurable value at all.
wrong.3: This assumes the small lines are only half the space, which is not true.
